solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Critical CERN act resolved — this'll go round the globe

indicators.note: a problem resolved is broken down and worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: Scientists at CERN resolve a critical experiment whose effects will be felt worldwide.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes the definition a whole phrase: a line of latitude really does go right round the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic Circle is a line of latitude encircling the Earth near the South Pole.

clue.text: Fully expert English PhD, claims local fake

indicators.note: a fake is a made-up version, so the letters are made into something else

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A local man boasts of an English doctorate that turns out to be bogus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fully expert' reads as praise for the PhD holder, but it is the definition; 'fake' at the end sits after its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all-accomplished is skilled in every respect, that is, fully expert.

clue.text: Retaliation from Italian stronghold in shelled state

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
a shelled thing has its outer casing removed, so the word state loses its first and last letters

parts.note: with its outer letters stripped away, state leaves its middle three letters
a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: Someone is fleeing an Italian fortress in a war-torn, bombarded country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' looks like bombardment, but it strips the outside letters of 'state' to leave TAT, which then wraps around IT and FORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is an idiom for paying back an injury with an equivalent one, which is exactly what retaliation means.

clue.text: Breach of trust at last entering clean sport after exchange

indicators.note: after exchange means the two pieces swap places, the sport coming before the clean word

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: entering means the letter goes inside the clean word

parts.note: pure means clean

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of trust

explanation.surface: A breach of confidence finally pollutes a clean sport after a transfer deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Clean sport would read PURE RU; 'after exchange' swaps the two, and T goes into PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture is a break or breach, as in a relationship or a pipe.

clue.text: Unspoken diplomacy surrounding India

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it, so the word for diplomacy encloses the letter

parts.note: tact is diplomacy
India is I in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Quiet diplomatic manoeuvring around India.
explanation.walkthrough: India is the NATO alphabet's word for I, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken.

clue.text: Clear the ground around wide part of vehicle

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters go around the single letter for wide
ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters of these words are crushed and reshaped

parts.note: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear an area of land around a broad section of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the noun earth, but it is grind's past tense: CLEAR and THE rearranged give CARTHEEL, and W for wide goes inside. A wide is a ball bowled out of a batter's reach in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is the wooden wheel of a cart, so it is literally a component of that vehicle.

clue.text: Having no time at all, dump Rod's port

indicators.note: having no means the time letter is removed
at all means every instance goes, here both letters standing for time

parts.note: tip is British for a rubbish dump
a switch is a thin rod or cane; the 's is a link
T is the abbreviation for time; both Ts are removed

explanation.surface: Pressed for time, someone abandons Rod's harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: TIP and SWITCH each lose their T, leaving IP and SWICH. A tip is British for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich is a port town in Suffolk, on the estuary of the River Orwell.

clue.text: Break Dave's sidekick before Mike

indicators.note: before means in front of, so the sidekick is written ahead of the letter for Mike

parts.note: Chas and Dave were a London singing duo
Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A friend's sidekick gets a break ahead of Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a Cockney pub-rock duo from London, so Dave's partner is Chas.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep break or gap, in rock or in relations.

clue.text: Former US prison service voided a Conservative peer's charge sheets?

parts.note: ex means former
pen is American slang for a penitentiary

indicators.note: service emptied of its middle leaves S and E

parts.note: the outer letters of SErvicE
taken as it stands
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a count is a peer, so peer's is COUNT'S

explanation.surface: An American prison service drops charges against a Tory lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge sheets' sounds like police paperwork; the question mark flags a pun on charges as costs billed to an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Expense accounts are records of costs charged to an employer, so sheets of charges.

clue.text: Stop extremely loathsome set from the east

indicators.note: only the extremes, first and last letters, of loathsome are used

parts.note: the outer letters of LoathsomE

indicators.note: in an across clue, read from the east means right to left

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A horrid group from the east is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' could be a noun, a group, which the surface wants; it is the verb, giving PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: rain that lets up stops, or at least eases off.

clue.text: Second mouth organ found on witty guy who deals illegally?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who deals illegally', the noun the answer is

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a card is a witty or eccentric person
S is the abbreviation for second
a harp is slang for a harmonica, or mouth organ

explanation.surface: A comedian with a harmonica is suspected of dodgy dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun on 'deals': a card-sharp deals cards dishonestly, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-sharp cheats at cards, dealing illegally.

clue.text: Game for abandoning cold blue cheese

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: the word for is abandoned, dropping out of the cheese's name

parts.note: Roquefort is a French blue cheese made from ewe's milk

explanation.surface: A sporting event is staged for the sake of giving up chilled blue cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word, but it is the letters taken out of ROQUEFORT, leaving ROQUET; C goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn sport in which mallets drive balls through hoops.

clue.text: Jot piece for US poet

parts.note: a jot and a whit both mean a tiny amount
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Someone scribbles a short piece for an American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jot' is a noun here, not the verb 'write quickly', which is what the writing surface wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman was a nineteenth-century American poet, author of Leaves of Grass.

clue.text: Mobile home agent working as a solicitor

indicators.note: mobile letters move about and rearrange

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: An estate agent selling mobile homes moonlights as a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A solicitor is a British lawyer, which the surface wants, but here it is someone soliciting on the street; 'on the game' is British slang for working as a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the game is to work as a prostitute, one who solicits for clients.

clue.text: Plant in Beirut, capital, regularly damaged

indicators.note: the combined letters are broken up and put back together in a new order
taking letters at regular intervals here means the second, fourth and sixth letters of capital

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of capital

explanation.surface: A plant growing in a war-damaged Lebanese capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'capital' are AIA; with BEIRUT, rearranged, they spell the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrietia is a trailing rock-garden perennial with purple flowers, a common garden plant.

clue.text: Harbour almost brings in European haul

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the shortened harbour word holds the letter
'almost' cuts a letter off

parts.note: HAVEN is what 'Harbour' stands for
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A port nearly takes in a European catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' could be the verb, to shelter; it is the noun, a haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: sailors heave on a rope and haul on it alike, pulling with effort.

clue.text: I draw Romeo, nailed by a dry performer

indicators.note: something nailed by others is held fast between them, so the Romeo letter sits inside

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry
an actor is a performer
R is Romeo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a Romeo caught by a sober thespian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests sketching, but here it means pull towards: the answer speaks of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractor is something that pulls other things towards it, as a magnet attracts iron.

clue.text: Excessive work held back primate

indicators.note: held back means turned backwards

parts.note: OTT is over the top
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Excess work held back a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A potto is a slow-moving African primate.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a small nocturnal primate of African forests.

clue.text: Old wild ass pulled up herb

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means reading upward

parts.note: an onager is an Asian wild ass

explanation.surface: An old wild donkey is pulled up by the herb patch.
explanation.walkthrough: The onager is a crossword favourite for wild ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a culinary herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Projectile is following line into sea

indicators.note: into means the letters go inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe

indicators.note: following means is comes after the letter for line

explanation.surface: A missile follows a line into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projectile' reads as a noun but is the adjective: hurled or propelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistic describes the flight of thrown or fired missiles, so it is an adjective for objects in motion through the air.

clue.text: Foolish mother leaves in a manner of speaking

parts.note: an idiomatic expression is a manner of speaking; the mother's letters sit in its middle
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A silly mother walks out, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a hedging phrase; it defines IDIOMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: an idiotic plan and a foolish plan are the same thing.

clue.text: Serial killer's second, false, nationality

indicators.note: false signals the letters of serial are not in their true order
second means the second letter of killer's

explanation.surface: A serial killer's second identity is a fake nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Israeli is the nationality of a citizen of Israel.

clue.text: Dress suggestively revealing half of girdle?

indicators.note: revealing, in this down clue, shows the kept letters read upwards, from bottom to top
half of means only the first half of girdle is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a girdle is a corset; its first half is kept
suggestively stands for the upward direction word that, in a down light, would signal the reading backwards; the answer spells that signal out

explanation.surface: A saucy hint of a corset seen from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, UP is a signal to read letters backwards; here the answer contains that signal, so the first half of 'girdle' written UP is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig up is to dress or kit out, as in rigged up in costume.

clue.text: Marx brother takes in Silver City

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the brother's name holds the metal's symbol

parts.note: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Marx brother goes to see a film called Silver City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver City' reads as one name; the two words split, silver the wordplay and City the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chicago, on Lake Michigan, is the third-largest city in the US.

clue.text: Run into something with teeth — one little dog

indicators.note: running into something here means going inside it, so the letter for run sits within the toothed thing

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a creature with teeth, just a little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something with teeth' sounds like the dog itself, but it is a cog.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small short-legged dog.

clue.text: Delivered welcome change where sacrifices maybe made

indicators.note: delivered as in spoken, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome; to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A welcome change of scene has been handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, HI ALTER gives HIGH ALTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A high altar is the chief altar of a church, and altars are traditionally the place of offering.

clue.text: Giant artist missing an island

indicators.note: the artist is missing the I

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian painter
I is the abbreviation for island; remove it from TITIAN

explanation.surface: A great painter is missing an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Either I of TITIAN may go; the second leaves TITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, from the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: New unopened iPod with plastic micro CD

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
unopened means the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A shopping list of gadgets: a sealed music player and a tiny plastic disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CD' looks like a compact disc, but it is the abbreviation of corps diplomatique.
explanation.definitionFit: CD stands for corps diplomatique, the body of ambassadors and envoys posted to a country.
